chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: Jamming with Chu Berry in Seattle and the union fine threat
summary: Cole and Chu sat in at a club in Seattle while with Cab and nearly got fined $500.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Oh boy, he could swing, that's the thing, see just anything. Tell you what we did. We were working the Palomar Theatre in Seattle, Washington, with Cab. And

this woman came by, she owned this club, and wanted if Chu and I could come on out there and play. You know, jam, which is all right, we didn't think too much of jamming in those days. We didn't care too much, didn't care. So anyway we went out that night, you know, after you'd finished, I thought it was nice little band, we loved to sit in with the band, because they could play, you know, we got to know the boys. So, everything went well and we told the woman we'll be back Saturday, or whatever night it was. Okay. So whatever night it was, say Thursday or Saturday night, we promised the woman we'd be back, but that day, see Chu, Noah and myself had got the paper and we didn't see it advertised in the paper. You know Chu Berry and Cozy Cole are going to be at this club tonight. So we went out there that night, man, and played and had us a ball, we got a nice meal, you know, and boy we came back and boy, Cab was raising hell, the union. What the hell you guys doing, you know, playing competition against us. They were going to fine us $500 apiece and had Chu and I were frightened to death, but they didn't do it afterwards, but that stopped us from going around doing that, you know. Jamming. But, it was all in fun in those days, that's the learning period. When you say during those years, you know, you aren't married and you're having a ball, you know, you like to play, and a lot of things you do, I wouldn't think of doing some of the things I did then, but I think about doing them now.

Well going around jamming like that, you know. Because a lot of times you go around and jam and the man will just hire two or three pieces, because he knows within himself before the night's over, he's going to have eight or ten pieces. See and I don't mind going out and jamming if there's not a paid audience, you know, jamming around musicians or something.
